sources.entry: Bytebase - Safe database schema change and version control for DevOps teams, supports MySQL, PostgreSQL, TiDB, ClickHouse, and Snowflake. (Source Code) MIT Docker/K8S/Go

summary.one_liner: Bytebase is an open-source database governance platform that acts as a control plane for schema change management, access control, and compliance across multiple database engines.
summary.what_it_does: Bytebase provides a web console for requesting, reviewing, deploying, and rolling back database changes. It includes a SQL review feature with 200+ lint rules, native GitHub/GitLab integration for database-as-code workflows, and fine-grained project and workspace-level RBAC. It offers just-in-time time-boxed database access, dynamic column-level data masking, audit logging, and data classification. The README also describes an MCP server for AI agents, text-to-SQL in the SQL Editor, and a built-in AI assistant. It supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, MongoDB, Redis, MariaDB, TiDB, Snowflake, ClickHouse, Spanner, OceanBase, and others.
use_cases: Masking sensitive columns and auditing database access
Centralizing management of multiple database environments
how_to_run: Visit the web console and follow the setup wizard
notable: Single control plane for humans and AI agents to access databases, with change review and audit trail
Dynamic data masking applied at query time based on user role
Terraform Provider and API for codified policy
Supports a wide range of engines including Oracle, SQL Server, MongoDB, and Redis
caveats: Some features (such as the AI assistant, JIT access, or other advanced features) may depend on plan tiers; the README does not detail which features are paid
Contributing setup requires a local PostgreSQL database and Go/pnpm toolchain
Installation documentation is linked externally rather than included in the README
